title: ICU 3 North Charge Nurse: Blank Telemetry Displays and Pump Library Alert

transcript.speaker: Mara Voss
transcript.text: Carol, it's Mara Voss from ICU 3 North. I need to report something unusual on the central telemetry board.

transcript.speaker: Mara Voss
transcript.text: Four beds—3, 7, 9, and 12—are showing as blank. The bedside monitors still show normal waveforms, and no alarms are active.

transcript.speaker: Mara Voss
transcript.text: On bed 7, the infusion pump is displaying 'library update pending'—I've never seen that before. I'm not sure if it's a glitch or something more serious.

transcript.speaker: Mara Voss
transcript.text: Do I need to initiate a downtime procedure, or should I just wait and see if it resolves?

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Mara, keep the bedside alarms audible for all four patients. I’m on it.

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Call Clinical Engineering immediately. Ask them to confirm if other units have the same pump message.

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Also, tell the Nursing Supervisor to check all ICU and step-down units for blank displays or the same pump alert.

transcript.speaker: Mara Voss
transcript.text: Copy that, Carol. I’ll connect with CE now.

instructorNote: This is a inject. The CNO must escalate to Clinical Engineering and initiate system-wide checks for the pump library message. Watch for whether the CNO activates the EHR Downtime Procedures Annex (ORRMC-DT-ANX-2026) or calls for a formal incident declaration.
